data.description:
# Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported saturated

Close the last 12 `saturated`-without-live-work polls by making the proxy
annotate the slot it is still draining: every abandonment records a matchable
identity (or an endpoint-wide entry), so a draining slot reads
`abandoned_busy` and only genuinely live work reports `saturated`.

## Problem statement

The AC1 fix (`LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK`) took `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` from **247 polls
(2.12 %)** to **12 polls (0.11 %)** over a comparable 11 h night, but not to
zero. Every remaining violation is a *draining* slot: llama-server has been
told to stop (the upstream stream was closed) yet has not freed the slot, and
nothing annotates it — `local_abandoned_slots=0`, so the poll reads
`saturated` even though nothing the proxy is waiting for occupies the pool.

The gap is therefore an **annotation** gap, not a liveness gap: the proxy
knows it abandoned the work, but the status builder cannot tie that
abandonment to the slot the backend is still draining.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether
  the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a draining ghost
  misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker).
  `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a ghost-driven
  `saturated` causes avoidable paid fallback.
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`.
  Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is
  as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when the pool holds only work the proxy abandoned, I
  want `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` (not `saturated`) so I can tell "busy
  because of us" from "busy because of live work".
- As the routing policy, I want a draining slot to never look saturated, so a
  needless cloud fallback is not triggered by work nobody is waiting for.
- As an analyst, I want each draining-slot abandonment attributable to a slot
  or to its endpoint, so a re-measured residual can be explained rather than
  merely counted.

## Evidence (from the AC4 run, preserved)

Re-measurement `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`, night 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30
07:00, artifacts in `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`
(`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, 12 rows, all fresh detail):

| episode | polls | attribution | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-30 06:57:36 | 3 (one second) | unattributable | `measured_cache_deficit` release 31 s earlier; `available_slots=0 total_slots=2 local_abandoned_slots=0`; pool idle again by 06:57:43 |
| 2026-10-30 06:01:20–21 | 2 | unattributable | — |
| 2026-10-29 20:19:25 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 295 s |
| 2026-10-29 20:35:03 | 1 | `prefill_deadline` | 14 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:36:23 | 2 | `no_progress_watchdog` | 182 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:47:30–31 | 2 | `prefill_deadline` | 48 s |
| 2026-10-30 01:43:11 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 520 s |

Two shapes of the same gap:

1. **Attributable (7 polls)** — an abandonment whose cancel succeeded leaves a
   slot that is still `is_processing` but carries **no** abandoned-registry
   entry (`local_abandoned_slots=0`), so the annotation does not fire.
2. **Unattributable (5 polls)** — a release with no slot identity at all
   (`measured_cache_deficit` on a record without a pinned slot), so the poll
   cannot be attributed even with the 600 s lookback.

Two further observations to confirm during implementation (not yet claimed as
causes):

- two rows (06:01:20, 01:43:11) report `available_slots=1` **alongside**
  `saturated`, which a purely-occupied pool cannot produce;
- one row reports `latency_ms=3355`, above the `/slots` detail budget, while
  `slots_detail_stale=false`.

If either turns out to be a distinct (non-lag) defect, record it as a
`discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` item rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it
   gave up on, or records an explicit "unknown slot, endpoint-wide" entry that
   the status builder can match to a processing slot on that endpoint (so a
   release without a slot id is still annotatable).
2. A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`
   until llama-server reports it free (registry TTL keeps it bounded; no
   leaked marker, no double decrement, no phantom lease).
3. `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`
   and never `idle`; a genuinely live, proxy-owned slot still reports
   `saturated` (the truthful-status contract of `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` is not
   weakened).
4. Deterministic tests (mocked `/slots` snapshot, injected clock) cover both
   shapes above, including the case where the draining slot is visible in a
   *fresh* snapshot, the endpoint-wide (unknown-slot) match, and the negative
   case (endpoint-wide entry present but the slot is owned by a live dispatch
   record → still `saturated`).
5. Re-measurement over a comparable night shows **0** `saturated`-without-live-
   work polls (baseline for this residual: 12 polls / 0.11 %, of which 5
   unattributable).
6. Full suite green through the `test` skill; docs updated where the
   abandonment → capacity interaction is described
   (`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Truthful status is not weakened** (`LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM`): an endpoint-wide
  match must never annotate a slot that a live dispatch record owns, and a
  fresh snapshot with genuinely live decode work must keep reporting
  `saturated`.
- The registry stays **in-process**, keyed by `(endpoint, slot)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s default), no
  timer task, no unbounded growth. An endpoint-wide entry needs a key that
  cannot collide with a real slot id.
- The annotation is **read-only status decoration**: it must never free or
  acquire capacity, double-decrement counters, or create a phantom lease.
- The status schema stays **additive** (`status_schema_version` 4:
  `abandoned*`, `local_abandoned_slots`, `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy`).
- **Measurement must remain possible.** `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  `_ABANDON_REASONS` currently excludes `measured_cache_deficit`, so that
  release is reported unattributable no matter how well the proxy annotates
  it — the set must be extended (with a test) or AC5 is unmeasurable.
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Existing state

- Registry: `_abandoned_slots` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), keyed
  `(endpoint_or_empty, slot_id)`; `_record_abandoned_slot` returns `None` when
  the slot id is not an `int`, so an unknown-slot abandonment is silently
  dropped — this is exactly the shape-2 gap.
- Matching: `_abandoned_slot_for(slot_id, endpoint=…)` tries the exact
  endpoint, then the legacy/default endpoint, then any endpoint carrying that
  slot id. There is no endpoint-wide (slot-less) match.
- Recording paths: `_release_unserved_dispatch` resolves the slot via
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup` *before* freeing the assignment (prefill deadline,
  client disconnect); session eviction resolves one slot per released record
  in `proxy/proxy/server.py`; the watchdog and orphan sweep record too.
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` passes **neither** slot id nor
  stream, which is the shape-2 source.
- Status builder: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` annotates `abandoned`,
  `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_at_seconds_ago`
  when the registry matches the slot id; `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0
  returns `abandoned_busy` when every generating slot is abandoned and keeps
  `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
- Residual behaviour: the 7 attributable polls reported
  `local_abandoned_slots=0` while a slot was `is_processing`, so the recorded
  identity did not match the draining slot (stale/mis-resolved id, or a slot
  the backend reassigned after the free) and the annotation never fired.
- Docs already describe the mechanism in
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (§ *Abandoned work*) and
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ *Abandoned local dispatches*).

## Desired change

1. Every abandonment path records either the slot it gave up on (resolved
   before the assignment is freed, and re-verified against the slot the
   backend actually reports) or an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry.
2. The status builder matches an endpoint-wide entry only to a processing slot
   on that endpoint that no live dispatch record owns, so the draining ghost is
   annotated and live work is not.
3. The annotation survives until llama-server reports the slot free (or the TTL
   elapses), and is dropped when the slot is observed free; re-abandoning
   refreshes it; no duplicate entries, no leak.
4. `capacity_hint` for a pool whose only work is draining stays
   `abandoned_busy` — never `saturated`, never `idle`.
5. `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` counts a `measured_cache_deficit`
   release as an abandonment event for attribution, with a test.
6. Docs updated where the abandonment → capacity interaction is described.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — abandoned-slot registry, release paths,
  endpoint-wide entry, slot re-verification.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status slot builder, endpoint-wide match,
  `compute_capacity_hint` (rule 0 unchanged in intent).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload
  (`local_abandoned_slots`).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — session-eviction slot resolution (if the recorded
  identity needs re-verification).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — registry, annotation and
  capacity-hint tests for both shapes.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — status payload contract.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — attribution set.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 7 attributable residuals are identity/matching failures,
  not TTL expiry — the longest release→poll gap observed is 520 s against a
  900 s TTL. Verify by logging the recorded slot id against the processing slot
  id during implementation.
- **Assumption:** AC5 (night re-measurement) is an operational run after
  deploy, mirroring the parent's child `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the plan step may
  decompose it into a follow-on child instead of blocking the code change.
- **Risk:** an endpoint-wide match annotates live work → weakens the truthful
  contract. Mitigation: require no live dispatch record for that slot, and
  cover the negative case with a deterministic test (AC4).
- **Risk:** a slot reported free and immediately reassigned could inherit a
  stale endpoint-wide entry. Mitigation: clear the entry on an observed free
  slot and keep the bounded TTL.
- **Risk (scope creep):** cooldown behaviour (`prefill_thrash_cooldown`) and
  the two anomalous rows (`available_slots=1`, 3.3 s latency) are **out of
  scope** here; record them as `discovered-from` items if confirmed.
- **Risk:** extending `_ABANDON_REASONS` changes the historical baseline
  (247 / 12 poll counts were computed with the narrower set). Mitigation: state
  the change in the report note and in the docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB` — parent: abandoned local dispatches leave
  llama-server busy (completed).
- `LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK` — AC1: abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel
  (completed; this item closes its residual).
- `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037` — AC4: re-measure one comparable night (completed;
  produced the 12-poll baseline).
- `LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2` — regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported
  saturated (completed).

# Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path

## Summary

Make every abandonment path either name the slot the backend is still draining
or record an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry, so nothing the proxy
gave up on is ever unattributable.

Parent: LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — AC1, AC2, and the annotation half of AC3.

## Target outcome

A draining slot the proxy abandoned is *always* matchable from the registry:
the 7 attributable-but-unannotated polls (shape 1) and the 5 unattributable
`measured_cache_deficit` polls (shape 2) both gain a registry entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it** gave up on, or an endpoint-wide entry the status builder can match.
- **AC2 — A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`** until llama-server reports it free, TTL-bounded, no leak.
- `_record_abandoned_slot` no longer silently drops an abandonment: an
  unresolvable slot identity records an endpoint-wide entry (a documented
  sentinel key that cannot collide with an `int` slot id) carrying
  `slot_id=None`, `endpoint`, `session_id`, `reason`, `abandoned_at`,
  `ttl_seconds` and a `scope` field (`"slot"` | `"endpoint"`).
- Every recording path reaches that behaviour: prefill deadline, client
  disconnect, no-progress watchdog, orphan sweep, session eviction and the
  measured-cache-deficit abort (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, which
  currently passes neither slot id nor stream). A test asserts an entry exists
  for each path when the slot is unresolvable.
- `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` forwards the dispatch record's
  pinned slot identity (and its `stream_cm`) instead of relying on a
  post-free session lookup, so the upstream cancel and the annotation both
  fire on the earliest-abort path.
- The resolved id is re-verified against the slot the backend actually reports
  (session/record binding captured *before* the assignment is freed). On
  mismatch the release logs `abandoned_slot_mismatch` with
  `recorded_slot=`, `observed_slot=` and still records the endpoint-wide
  entry, so shape 1 becomes diagnosable rather than silent.
- Log lines carry `slot_source=explicit|assignment|endpoint_wide` so the
  intake OPEN QUESTION ("why did the 7 attributable polls show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`") is answerable from production logs.
- Registry invariants hold: in-process, keyed `(endpoint, key)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s), no timer
  task, re-abandoning refreshes, entry count bounded by `(endpoint, slot)`
  pairs plus one endpoint-wide entry per endpoint.
- The annotation path still never frees/acquires capacity, decrements counters
  or creates a lease (assert in tests).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: add the endpoint-wide sentinel and a
  `scope` field in `_record_abandoned_slot`; record instead of returning
  `None`; extend `_abandoned_slot_lookup`/`_release_unserved_dispatch` to
  capture the record's pinned slot before the free and to log
  `slot_source`; keep `_abandoned_slot_for` exact-match precedence.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: pass the record slot + `stream_cm` from
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`: session-eviction slot capture already resolves per
  record — route it through the same "record or endpoint-wide" helper so an
  unresolvable record still annotates.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Deterministic tests: endpoint-wide abandonment annotation**
  (test first, then this item makes them pass).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — registry, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_for`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `session_evicted` slot resolution
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline/measured-cache abort call sites
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — path coverage

# Goal

Author the **red-first** test suite that encodes the new `/slots` read-path contract *before* any
implementation, so every implementation child in this plan is driven by failing tests rather than
written first and tested afterwards.

These tests pin the behaviour that makes `slots_stale` measurable and small: one bounded upstream
fetch per refresh cycle, a snapshot-age freshness definition, and untouched reconciliation
guarantees for `capacity_hint`.

# Test matrix

1. **Fan-out.** N concurrent `GET /llama/local/status` polls inside the freshness window issue
   **exactly one** upstream `/slots` request. Extend the existing coalescing suite rather than
   writing a second harness.
2. **Latency bound.** With an injected backend that never answers, the status handler returns
   within the configured budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) plus a small slack — it must not serialise
   counts (2 s) + detail (1 s) + status (1 s) awaits.
3. **Age-derived freshness.** A table-driven test asserts `slots_stale` follows the published
   snapshot age versus the freshness budget: `age < budget ⇒ false`, `age == budget ⇒ false`,
   `age > budget ⇒ true`, and `missing snapshot ⇒ true`.
4. **Additive schema.** A consumer that ignores unknown fields sees unchanged `available_slots` /
   `total_slots` / `slots` semantics; the payload carries the versioned schema field.
5. **Stale reconciliation unchanged.** For every stale-snapshot fixture, `capacity_hint` is never
   `saturated` while `local_in_flight_requests == 0` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM AC3 must survive this
   change).
6. **Log compatibility.** The `status_request` line gains per-phase timing fields additively;
   the existing parsers (`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
   `proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py`) keep parsing unchanged lines.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The new/updated tests exist and **fail (red)** against current `dev` for the fan-out,
  latency-bound and age-derivation assertions, and the failing run summary is recorded on this item.
- AC2: The fan-out test asserts an exact upstream call count of 1 for 5 concurrent polls inside the
  freshness window (not a `<=` bound).
- AC3: The hang-injection test asserts handler wall-clock latency `< budget + 250 ms` when `/slots`
  never responds.
- AC4: The age-derivation table covers `< budget`, `== budget`, `> budget` and missing-snapshot
  cases, one assertion each.
- AC5: Stale-reconciliation regression tests assert `capacity_hint != "saturated"` whenever
  `local_in_flight_requests == 0` across all stale fixtures.
- AC6: The suite goes green after the implementation children land **without editing these tests**
  (no test rewrites to chase the implementation).

# Key Files:

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py`

# Reuse

- Existing coalescing/single-flight harness (`_fetch_slots_payload`, LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT tests).
- Existing stale-reconciliation fixtures in `test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`.

## Goal

Write the failing tests for the **release→backend-cancel joiner** before it
exists, so "the proxy released a dispatch and llama-server kept prefilling"
becomes a measured, per-dispatch fact instead of the subtraction of two
unrelated counters.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2 (and the instrument AC1 needs).

## Target outcome

A hermetic fixture pair (a proxy-log slice plus the matching
`llama-server.log` slice) and a test module that pin the joiner's contract.
The tests fail until the implementation item lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fixture pair is committed and hermetic.** `proxy/tests/fixtures/`
  holds a proxy-log slice and a `llama-server.log` slice covering the same
  fake window, containing all four shapes: (a) release → backend cancel → N
  `prompt processing progress` lines → `slot release: … stop processing`;
  (b) release with **no** observed backend cancel; (c) release whose cancel
  exists but cannot be joined to a task id; (d) a cancelled task that *still*
  emitted `prompt eval time`. No live `llama-server`, no `/var/log` access.
- **AC2 — Per-release columns are asserted.** For every release the joiner
  reports: release reason, proxy release timestamp, joined
  `id_task` (or `unjoined`), whether a cancel was observed, the number of
  `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, the cancel→`stop
  processing` latency in seconds, and whether `prompt eval time` was emitted
  for that task.
- **AC3 — Unjoined is reported, never dropped.** A test asserts every release
  appears exactly once in the output, with unjoinable ones counted as
  `unjoined` and carrying a machine-readable reason; the sum of
  joined + unjoined equals the release count.
- **AC4 — No fabricated cancels.** A test asserts the joiner reports **no**
  cancel for shape (b), so a naive time-window join cannot pass by marking
  everything cancelled.
- **AC5 — Distributions are reported, not point estimates.** The cancel→`stop
  processing` latency is reported as p10/p50/p90, and tokens evaluated after
  the cancel are counted from the fixture's progress lines — not derived from
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`.
- **AC6 — Test module runs green in isolation and in the suite.**
  `python -m pytest proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py`
  collects and (post-implementation) passes; the module needs no network, no
  GPU and no live proxy.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_proxy.log` — real
   `local_eviction_after_acceptance` / `lease_released` / `abandoned_slot_recorded`

2. Add `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_llama.log` — real
   llama-server line shapes (`srv stop: cancel task, id_task = N`,

   `slot release: … stop processing`, `prompt eval time = …`).
3. Write `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py` importing the
   analyser the same way `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
   does (add `proxy/scripts` to `sys.path`, `importlib.import_module`).
4. Keep every assertion on the *contract* (columns, invariants, distributions),
   not on internal helper names.

- `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_proxy.log` — new fixture.

None — this is the first (test-first) slice.

## Goal

Write the failing tests for the **corrected abandoned-prefill window model**
before changing it, so the 58/60 overlap figure and the 667 s median backlog
can be restated on a measured basis while staying backwards comparable.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2, AC3 (measurement half).

## Target outcome

Tests that pin `abandoned_prefill_windows()` to the *observed* backend stop
(cancel → `slot release: … stop processing`) instead of
`tokens / ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`, including an explicit
"unbounded / legacy basis" fallback, dual-basis reporting, and the
zero-progress-while-draining count AC3's second half needs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window end comes from the observed stop.** A test asserts that when
  a cancel→`stop processing` pair is available for a released dispatch, the
  window's `end` is the observed stop time (within tolerance) and its
  duration is **not** the token/rate estimate; the row records which basis
  produced it.
- **AC2 — Unbounded windows are labelled, not invented.** When no stop is
  observed, a test asserts the row is marked `bounded=false` and carries the
  legacy token/rate estimate explicitly labelled as an estimate — the two
  bases are never mixed silently.
- **AC3 — Dual-basis reporting.** The overlap count/total for
  `prefill_deadline` events (the 58/60 figure) is computed on **both** bases
  (legacy estimator and measured), both are present in the report, and the
  report states which one the verdict uses.
- **AC4 — A retry inside a cancelled-and-stopped window is not "starved".** A
  fixture where the retry dispatch starts *after* the observed stop yields
  `abandoned_prefill_overlap=false`; a fixture where it starts *before* the
  stop yields `true` — so the metric can no longer count post-stop dispatches
  as starved.
- **AC5 — Zero-progress while draining is counted.** The report exposes a
  count of accepted dispatches that expired their lease with no
  `prefill_progress_measured` while their session's slot was still inside an
  abandoned window — the second half of AC3, reported separately from the
  share.
- **AC6 — Hermetic and isolated.** `python -m pytest
  proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_windows_measured.py` runs with no live
  logs; the existing suite test
  `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py` keeps passing.

   joiner fixture) with: measured stop present, stop absent, retry before stop,
   retry after stop, zero-progress lease inside a window.

   assertions on `abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backlog_evidence()` and the

None (test-first). Sibling of the joiner test item; both feed the analyser
implementation item.

## Goal

Make every proxy release of an accepted local dispatch **attributable to a
backend task lifecycle**, and correct the abandoned-prefill window model, so
"prefills computed and thrown away" is a measurement rather than the
subtraction of two counters.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2 (the instrument), with the model correction
AC1 needs and AC5's docstring requirement.

## Target outcome

`proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` (or a sibling module it
imports) joins `local_eviction_after_acceptance` / `lease_released` events to
`llama-server.log` task lifecycles over a ≥24 h restart-segmented window and
reports: releases with no explained backend stop (count + share), the
cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, tokens evaluated after the
cancel, and unjoined releases. The abandoned-prefill windows are derived from
observed stops, with the legacy token/rate basis retained for comparability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Release→cancel accounting exists and is produced from on-disk logs
  only.** A function (e.g. `release_cancel_accounting(...)`) emits, per
  window: `releases_total`, `releases_with_observed_cancel`,
  `releases_without_explained_backend_stop` (count and share),
  `releases_unjoined` (count and per-event reason), `cancel_to_stop_seconds`
  p10/p50/p90, and `tokens_evaluated_after_cancel` (totals and per-event).
- **AC2 — CLI exposure.** The script gains a documented way to point at the
  `llama-server` log(s) for a window (reusing/extending `--llama-log`) and
  emits the accounting in the JSON dataset; `--json` output stays
  machine-parseable and the text summary states the accounting headline.
- **AC3 — Nothing is dropped.** Every release appears exactly once: joined,
  unjoined-with-reason, or explained-by-another-mechanism. The sums are
  asserted by the sibling test item.
- **AC4 — Window model corrected, both bases kept.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`
  derives each window's end from the observed backend stop when one exists and
  marks the row `bounded=true/false`; `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S` remains
  available as the legacy basis, and the report carries both the legacy and
  corrected overlap counts for `prefill_deadline` events (so 58/60 can be
  restated on both bases).
- **AC5 — Docstring tells the truth.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`'s
  docstring no longer asserts "a released dispatch is **not** cancelled at
  `llama-server`"; it states what is measured, what is estimated, and the
  provenance of each constant.
- **AC6 — Tests from both test-first items pass**; `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
  keeps passing unchanged; the full suite is green through `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Parse `llama-server.log` lines into task-lifecycle records: `launch_slot_`
  (slot/task), `update_slots … prompt processing progress` (`n_tokens`,
  `batch.n_tokens`, `progress`), `srv stop: cancel task, id_task = N`,
  `slot release: … stop processing`, `prompt eval time`.
2. Join each release to a task by (a) `llama_task_id`/`slot_id` when the log
   line carries them, else (b) the session's slot at release + nearest
   preceding `launch_slot_` for that slot; record how each join was made and
   count the unjoined residue.
3. Emit the accounting block in `build_report()` and the text summary.
4. Re-point `abandoned_prefill_windows()` at observed stops, keeping the
   legacy estimate under an explicit `bounded=false` label, and have
   `backlog_evidence()`/`attribute_events()` report both bases.
5. Rewrite the `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring per AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

data.description:
## Goal

**As an** operator running unattended `local-preferred` (pin-local) herdr workers,
**I want** the local prefill-thrash cooldown to expire in ~2 minutes instead of 10,
**so that** a single measured cold-prefix abort costs a pinned session a short retry
window rather than a ten-minute `429 Local admission refused` lockout, while
keeping the measured-cache early abort (F3, `LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN`) fully in force.

Operator decision 2026-10-31: this is the approved **interim** mitigation (of the
three options put to the operator, option B — the config-only change; option "A"
raising `local_measured_cache_abort_bound_tokens` / disabling the abort was
rejected because a 23-34 k prompt would then pay a 62-200 s prefill against a
120 s deadline, restoring the deadline-eviction thrash F3 exists to prevent, and
option "C" dropping the `local-preferred` pin was rejected because it cannot help
in the 06:00-10:00 UTC remote hole — see `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135` and the new
structural-unavailability item).

discovered-from:LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135 (the defect that keeps the abort armed),
discovered-from:LP-0MVR7HJD0007RFEM (Option D / measured-cache abort epic).

## Observed incident (2026-10-31, herdr session `herdr-1793416360-4155786-6690`)

Diagnosis via the `proxy-log-skill`. The pane was dispatched pinned
(`X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, `preference=local-preferred` on every
proxy line). Over 7 h 47 m it produced **~15 local turns and 113 refusals**
(100 x `429 Local admission refused`, plus `503`s). Refusal reasons for this one
session today:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| `local_provider_cooldown` | 83 |
| `local_route_unavailable` | 13 |
| `prefill_thrash_cooldown` | 11 |
| `local_lease_active` | 5 |
| `eta_exceeds_budget` | 1 |

Every refusal cycle began with one abort that armed the cooldown:

```
08:16:32  measured_cache_abort session=herdr-1793416360-... total=23164 cache=0
          measured_new_tokens=23164 priced_new_tokens=2198 deficit_ratio=1.0
          bound_tokens=2000 elapsed_s=0.1 → cancelling local dispatch early
08:16:32  prefill_thrash_cooldown_started session=... cooldown_s=600
08:16:32  local_eviction ... reason=lease_evicted
… then, for the next 600 s, every retry:
          local_only_refused reason=local_provider_cooldown preference=local-preferred
          verdict=deferrable ... route=refused
          local_preference_resolved ... outcome=pinned
```

The session then sat in a 600 s refusal window, retrying roughly once a minute,
and was released only when the cooldown lapsed and the slot happened to still
hold its prefix (`07:07`, `10:57-10:58` produced the real turns).

Scope of the problem: **330 `measured_cache_abort` events across 28 sessions**
today, **249 of them at `deficit_ratio=1.0`** (cache entirely gone). Per hour:
05 h 82, 10 h 62, 04 h 51, 09 h 34, 07 h 31, 08 h 28. At 600 s per abort this is
the dominant source of pinned-client refusals on this host.

## Why 600 s is the wrong value here — and why this is a config change, not a rewrite

`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` is documented in `proxy/config.yaml`
(~:2087-2100) as the quarantine armed after a measured-cache-deficit abort. Its
intent is to stop a session thrashing the GPU with repeated cold prefill attempts.
But a cold-prefix abort costs ~0.1 s (the abort fires on the first
`prompt_progress` event), while the cooldown it arms costs 600 s of *client*
downtime — a 6000x asymmetry. For a pinned client, which by contract receives
`429` rather than a remote fallback, that asymmetry converts a 0.1 s GPU saving
into a 10-minute outage.

The measured recovery time for the same session shows 600 s buys nothing: after
the cooldown lapses the prefix is still cold (`cache=0` again at 08:27, 08:37,
08:48, 08:58, 09:09) — the thrash defence does not protect the cache, it only
delays the next attempt. 120 s still suppresses a genuine retry storm (the
observed client retry cadence is ~60 s) while capping the outage at two minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (value).** `server.local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` is `120` in
  `proxy/config.yaml`. No other cooldown, budget, deadline or abort knob changes
  value (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_bound_tokens: 2000`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_min_deficit_ratio: 0.25`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: true` all unchanged), asserted by a
  config test so an accidental re-tune is caught.
- **AC2 (armed duration).** The cooldown armed by a measured-cache-deficit abort
  is driven by that key, not by a literal: a unit/integration test sets the key
  to a distinctive value (e.g. `45`) and asserts
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started ... cooldown_s=45`, and that the local route
  is skipped with `reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` for that duration and no
  longer. No hard-coded `600` remains anywhere in the abort/cooldown path.
- **AC3 (defence retained).** The cooldown still *starts* on every
  `measured_cache_abort` (the thrash defence is not weakened, only shortened):
  the incident replay fixture asserts exactly one
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started` per abort, with `cooldown_s=120` at default
  configuration.
- **AC4 (abort behaviour unchanged).** `measured_cache_abort` decisions,
  `local_eviction_after_acceptance` fields and the warm-path contract are
  untouched: the existing `measured_cache_abort`, warm-path and replay tests
  pass unmodified. `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` still restores
  pre-change behaviour exactly.
- **AC5 (docs).** The `proxy/config.yaml` comment block for
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` record the
  new default, the 2026-10-31 operator decision, the 0.1 s-vs-600 s asymmetry
  rationale, and that the real repair is the benefit gate in
  `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`, after which this value should be re-tuned upward
  (the item must leave a note saying so, not silently imply 120 is permanent).

## Out of scope

- The benefit gate that stops the abort firing for prompts that fit the budget —
  `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`.
- Bounding the number of pin-local refusals / escalating to remote —
  `LP-0MVUH9PL0005PW90`.
- The 06:00-10:00 UTC `model=plan` remote hole and its client-facing error.
- Slot-prefix stability (why the prefix is cold at all).

## Key files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `server.local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` (~:2100),
  comment block (~:2087-2100).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — thrash-cooldown arm/release helpers.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — the decision (read-only here).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Assumptions

- 120 s is long enough to suppress the observed retry storm (client cadence
  ~60 s) and short enough that a pinned client recovers without operator help.
- Shortening the cooldown does not increase abort frequency in a way that costs
  more GPU time than it saves: each abort still costs ~0.1 s and the 120 s gap
  is two client retry intervals.
data.title: Interim: cut local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds 600s -> 120s so a pinned session's cold-prefix abort costs 2 minutes, not 10

## Goal

**As** the implementer of the measured-cache benefit gate, **I want** the
decision-level rows for the gate written and failing first, **so that** the
gate's continue/abort verdicts, its comparator budget and its input provenance
are pinned before any production code changes.

Parent AC1, AC10, and the unit half of AC6. **Test-first**: this item precedes
the decision implementation (the `[impl]` benefit-gate item depends on it).

## Scope

Add the benefit-gate rows to `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py`
(split into a sibling module only if that file becomes uncomfortable to read).
Every row **names its rate basis** in its docstring/assertion message (parent
AC1), so a future recalibration that re-breaks the incident fails loudly rather
than silently.

Determinism: clear/seed the rolling calibration through `proxy.prefill_eta.reset()`
and synthetic observed samples (the `_seed_varied` pattern in
`proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py`). The "shipped default fit" row
relies on the **uncalibrated** default `DEFAULT_PREFILL_MS_PER_TOKEN = 3.9`
(14 380 × 3.9 ms = 56.08 s), so it needs no seeded window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — incident row (parent AC1(a); D2 → `abort=False`).**
  `total=14380 cache=0 priced_new_tokens=48`, shipped config (uncalibrated
  default fit) ⇒ `abort=False`, `detail="within_eta_budget"`,
  `measured_eta_s ≈ 56.1` (±0.5 s), `budget_s == 114.0`. The docstring records
  the measured host range (38.8 s at 371 tok/s … 84.6 s at 170 tok/s) and an
  accompanying assertion shows the row still continues at the p25 rate
  (84.6 s < 114 s).
- **AC2 — huge-prompt row (parent AC1(b)).** `total=56000 cache=0
  priced_new_tokens≈100` (seeded so the p75 uplift applies) ⇒ `abort=True`,
  `detail="deficit_over_bound"` — today's behaviour preserved for the
  population the feature exists for. Both the shipped default fit (218.4 s)
  and the measured median (150.9 s) are recorded in the test and both exceed
  the 114 s comparator.
- **AC3 — the comparator is the prefill-deadline budget (D1).** Three rows:
  (i) `budget_safety_fraction=0` ⇒ `budget_s == local_prefill_deadline_seconds`
  (120 s) and the AC1 row still continues; (ii) a deadline tuned low enough to
  make the incident prompt exceed the comparator (e.g.
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 40` ⇒ 38 s) ⇒ `abort=True`, proving the
  comparator is deadline-derived; (iii) the admission wait budget never decides
  the verdict — with `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30` (and a
  `budget_seconds=30`-shaped admission evidence) the AC1 row still continues.
- **AC4 — gate input provenance (parent AC10).** With `priced_new_tokens=48`
  and `total=14380 cache=0`, `measured_eta_s >= 30` (the measured-rate floor),
  never ≈8 s; a companion assertion feeds `48` as though it were the measured
  deficit and asserts both `measured_eta_s` and the verdict change — so the
  optimism inversion that caused the incident cannot be reintroduced through
  the gate's input.
- **AC5 — fail-open on a missing budget (parent AC6).** Absent, `0`, negative,
  non-numeric or otherwise unreadable `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` /
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction`, a non-mapping config, and an
  unusable ETA estimator each resolve to `abort=False` with a `detail` that is
  **not** `deficit_over_bound`; a missing budget never manufactures an abort.
- **AC6 — existing decision rows unchanged.** Every pre-existing row in
  `test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` (warm path, ratio floor,
  monotonicity, `enabled` spellings, malformed config, never-raises) passes;
  only rows whose expectation the gate genuinely changes may be updated, and
  each such update carries an inline comment explaining why.
- **AC7 — the changed-scope test gate is green** (`/skill:test`, changed
  scope).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` — the decision rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — calibration seeding/reset
  pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — module under test.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `estimate_prefill_seconds` (`~893`),
  `_deadline_budget_seconds` (`~1293`), `DEFAULT_PREFILL_MS_PER_TOKEN` (`162`).

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the decision implementation.

## Deliverables

Decision tests that fail on today's code and encode the AC1(a)/AC1(b)/AC10/
AC6 verdicts, ready to be turned green by the implementation item.

## Goal

**As** an operator, **I want** the incident shape replayed end to end in the
test suite **so that** a pin-local prompt that fits the budget is served
locally with no thrash cooldown and no `429`, while a genuinely doomed prompt
keeps today's early detour.

Parent AC3, AC4, AC8, and the integration half of AC7. **Test-first**: written
before the wiring item, which depends on it.

Extend `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort_wiring.py` (release, cooldown and
eviction assertions) and `proxy/tests/measured_prefill_window_replay.py` (the
incident fixture), reusing the `proxy/tests/prefill_thrash_replay_harness.py`
style so the replay drives the real preview/peek path rather than a mock of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — incident replay fixture (parent AC8).** A fixture built from the five

data.description:
## Goal

As a drive operator, I want one shared, table-driven classifier that turns a
failing `finish` report into `{kind, step, reason, message}`, so `phase_drive`
can tell a transient infrastructure refusal from a genuine gate failure instead
of treating every failure as a gate failure (parent AC1).

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts through all layers end-to-end — the `finish`
subprocess's structured `steps` payload, `phase_parent._run_finish`'s report,
and the classifier `phase_drive` consumes — with unit tests and the reference
doc's vocabulary table updated in the same slice.

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - Add module-level constants **next to the emitters** (adjacent to
    `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` / `phase_finish`):
    - `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs (the
      allow-list from the parent item's **Assumptions**).
    - `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs for the
      known gate failures (`tests: tests_failed`, `build: build_failed`,
      `worktree_placement: *`, `diff: no_changes`, …) — recorded for
      documentation/consistency only; classification of anything not in
      either set is `unknown`.
    - `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS = ("infrastructure", "gate", "unknown")`.
  - Add `classify_finish_failure(finish_report: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]`
    returning `{kind, step, reason, message}`:
    - resolves `(step, reason)` from the report's structured `steps`
      (precedence: `main_checkout_lock` → `main_checkout_guard` →
      `local_dev_fast_forward` → `push` → `build` → `tests` →
      `ancestry_assertion`), never from prose;
    - `kind = "infrastructure"` only for an explicit allow-list hit;
      `"gate"` for an explicit gate-list hit; otherwise `"unknown"`
      (fail-safe: `unknown` is never `infrastructure`);
    - tolerates `None`, `{}` and non-dict input → `kind="unknown"`.
  - `phase_parent._run_finish`: call `_invoke_implement("finish", …, parse_on_failure=True)`
    and **keep the `None` sentinel** — `_run_finish` still returns `None` on
    failure, but records `report["finish_failure"] = classify_finish_failure(parsed)`
    on the parent report before returning.
  - Record a structured `steps` entry for the `finish` failure exits that have
    none today (the `AncestryAssertionError` handler ~6958 and the generic
    `RuntimeError` push/build/commit handlers), so classification never parses
    prose.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — seed the "Drive failure recovery"
  classification vocabulary table (completed in the docs item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One module-level vocabulary constant, colocated with the emitters,
   enumerates every `(step, reason)` pair the shipped `finish` code can emit;
   a table-driven test asserts the `kind` mapping for each entry.
2. A `(step, reason)` pair that is not listed classifies as `unknown`, never
   `infrastructure` (table-driven test covers the fail-safe direction).
3. `classify_finish_failure(None)`, `classify_finish_failure({})` and a
   non-dict argument each return `kind="unknown"` without raising.
4. `phase_parent._run_finish` invokes `finish` with `parse_on_failure=True`,
   still returns `None` on failure (sentinel pinned by a regression test), and
   the returned parent report carries `finish_failure` with the correct
   `step`/`reason`/`kind` for a scripted failing finish report.
5. Every `finish` failure exit that previously carried no structured `steps`
   entry (ancestry assertion, generic push failure, generic `RuntimeError`)
   records `{success: false, reason}` in `steps`, so no classification path
   depends on `report["message"]` prose.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC1 traceability.** **Single classifier for finish failures.** `phase_drive` classifies each failing `finish` as `infrastructure`, `gate` or `unknown` through one shared, table-driven classifier over an explicit `(step, reason)` vocabulary, derived from the `finish` subprocess report (threaded out of `phase_parent`'s `_run_finish`). Unit test: a table-driven test asserts the mapping for every refusal reason the shipped code can emit, and that an unlisted reason classifies as `unknown` (fail-safe, never `infrastructure`). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the three module-level constants beside `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`
   and `phase_finish`, with a comment stating the drift rule (a new `_refuse`
   reason must be added to the table in the same commit).
2. Write the failing table-driven test first (`TestFinishFailureClassifier`),
   enumerating the emitted pairs; then implement `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Thread `parse_on_failure=True` through `_run_finish`, keeping the `None`
   sentinel and adding `report["finish_failure"]`; add the sentinel regression
   test.
4. Add the missing structured `steps` entries in `phase_finish`'s failure
   exits; assert them in a test.
5. Seed the reference doc vocabulary table.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `classify_finish_failure` (new),
  `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS`
  (new), `phase_parent._run_finish` (~7558), `phase_finish` failure handlers
  (~6780–6980), `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` (~3595–3740).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Drive failure recovery" table.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Vocabulary drift** — a future `_refuse` reason is added and silently
  classifies as `gate`, re-creating the discard hazard. *Mitigation:* the
  constant sits next to the emitters; the table test enumerates every emitted
  pair; `unknown` fails safe.
- **`parse_on_failure=True` alters the placement-guard path.** *Mitigation:*
  the `None` sentinel is kept and pinned by a regression test.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice; every other child consumes
`classify_finish_failure` / `finish_failure`.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC1 (primary) — the single table-driven classifier; supplies the
`finish_failure` evidence payload that AC5's reporting slice consumes.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code
  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

data.description:
## Goal

As a maintainer writing the recovery tests, I want the drive test harness to
script finish failures **with a step and reason** and to provide a real
in-repo worktree that carries a commit ahead of the parent branch, so the
infra-retry, preservation-gate and gate-regression slices can each be pinned by
a deterministic test without touching production code (parent AC2, AC3, AC6).

Test-first item: it lands before the implementation slices that consume it.

## Scope

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`
  - Extend `finishing_failed_report(child_id, message=None, *, step=None,
    reason=None, kind=None)` so the emitted parent report carries the
    `finish_failure` payload produced by `classify_finish_failure`. Default
    arguments must reproduce today's report shape exactly (backwards
    compatible — existing callers unchanged).
  - Add a `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture: a real git repo with a `dev`
    branch plus a linked worktree whose branch holds one commit `dev` does not
    (and, separately, an uncommitted-only variant reusing the existing
    `child_worktree` fixture).
  - Add a `RecordingReset` / `recording_reset` helper that wraps
    `_reset_child_worktree` and records every call plus the git commands
    observed, so a test can assert "no destructive command ran".
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — only if the harness helpers are shared;
  keep changes additive.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `finishing_failed_report()` accepts `step`/`reason`/`kind` keyword
   arguments and emits a parent report whose `finish_failure` payload drives
   the production classifier to the expected `kind`; called with no extra
   arguments it emits byte-identical keys to today's helper.
2. A `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture creates a real repo + linked worktree
   whose `HEAD` is ahead of `dev`, and a meta-test asserts that setup (the
   ahead-of-parent relationship holds, and the commit is reachable).
3. A meta-test asserts the fixture's worktree is detected as "has changes"
   while a clean worktree at `dev` is not, so a later preservation test cannot
   pass vacuously.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator driving an epic unattended on a contended host, I want a
transient infrastructure refusal (`local_dev_diverged`, main-checkout lock
held, push transport drop) to be retried on its **own** bounded budget with
backoff instead of consuming the finish-attempt budget, so a refusal that
clears seconds later no longer discards a committed slice (parent AC2).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: classify `parent_report["finish_failure"]` on every
    `finishing_failed` report.
    - `kind == "infrastructure"` → increment `infra_retries[child]`, emit a
      `children_driven` entry with `result: "infra-retry"`, sleep the injected
      backoff, `continue` (re-run `parent`, which re-runs `finish`; **never**
      spawn a session). `finish_attempts[child]` is **not** incremented.
    - `kind in {"gate", "unknown"}` → existing bounded path unchanged.
  - New `--infra-retry-limit N` argparse flag (default `5`, non-positive
    clamped to 1) plumbed into `phase_drive` as `infra_retry_limit`.
  - New report keys: `infra_retries` (dict child → count),
    `infra_retry_limit` (int). Existing keys keep their meaning/types.
  - Backoff: `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` → `min(2 * 2**(attempt-1), 30)`
    seconds, with an injectable delay callable (`sleep`/`delay` parameter on
    `phase_drive`, default `time.sleep`) so tests pass a zero-delay recorder.
  - `max_iterations` bound accounts for `infra_retry_limit` so the loop still
    always terminates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `--infra-retry-limit` is present in `implement.py drive --help` and in the
   usage block; the default is `5`; a non-positive value is clamped to `1`.
2. An infrastructure refusal increments `infra_retries[child]` and leaves
   `finish_attempts` without an entry for that child (test asserts both).
3. Scripted harness returning three infrastructure refusals then success ends
   with `success: true`, the child recorded as `finished`,
   `infra_retries[child] == 3`, `infra_retry_limit == 5`, and
   `finish_attempts` empty for that child.
4. Each infrastructure retry emits a `children_driven` entry with
   `result: "infra-retry"` carrying `step`, `reason` and the attempt number,
   and spawns **no** session (`sessions_spawned` unchanged).
5. Exhausting `--infra-retry-limit` does not retry unboundedly: the loop falls
   through to the existing reconcile/reset path and stops with a message naming
   the failing `step` and `reason`.
6. The backoff schedule is bounded and injectable: a unit test asserts
   `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30]` seconds for attempts 1–6 and that no test sleeps.
7. `max_iterations` includes the infrastructure budget, and a
   always-refusing harness terminates (test in the regression item asserts the
   exact `parent` invocation count).
8. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
9. **Parent AC2 traceability.** **Infrastructure refusals do not consume the finish-attempt budget.** They are bounded separately by a new `--infra-retry-limit` (default `5`) with a bounded backoff between attempts; a refusal that clears within that budget lets the same `finish` succeed and the chain continue. Test: a scripted harness returning N infrastructure refusals then success ends with `success: true` and the child `finished`, and `finish_attempts` does **not** count the infrastructure attempts (`infra_retries` does). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the scripted-harness test first (3 infra refusals → success) against
   the extended harness from the test-harness item; it must fail.
2. Add `--infra-retry-limit` and `infra_retry_limit` plumbing plus report keys.
3. Branch on `finish_failure["kind"]` before the `finish_attempts` increment;
   emit `infra-retry`, record the delay, `continue`.
4. Add `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` and the injectable delay hook.
5. Extend `max_iterations`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` finish-failure branch
  (~8940–9100), `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` (new), `_emit_phase_report`
  (~8270), argparse block (~9630), usage block (~42).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — infra-retry budget tests.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — CLI-flag and loop-bound coverage.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Over-eager infrastructure classification hides a real gate failure.**
  *Mitigation:* explicit allow-list only (classifier item); `unknown` is never
  infrastructure; the budget is small and bounded; the chain still stops with
  the real reason.
- **Repeated retries re-run the changed-scope suite on a contended host.**
  *Mitigation:* default bound 5, exponential backoff capped at 30 s, no extra
  session spawn.

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading` — supplies
  `finish_failure` / `classify_finish_failure`.
- `Test harness: refusal scripting and commit-carrying worktree` — supplies the
  scripted `finish_failure` reports and the zero-delay recorder.

## Goal

As the owner of an already-committed child slice, I want drive to never
`reset --hard` a worktree that carries commits — parking the tip on a named
`refs/wip/<child-id>` instead — so my work cannot be discarded (parent AC3).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_reset_child_worktree(worktree_path, parent_branch=..., child_id="")`
    gains a **pre-destructive preservation gate** that runs after the existing
    isolation gates (linked-worktree check, `--show-toplevel` match) and
    **before** any `git reset --hard` / `git clean -fd`:
    - compute `git -C <wt> rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` (fall back
      to `merge-base --is-ancestor <parent_branch> HEAD`);
    - when the worktree is ahead of the parent branch: create
      `refs/wip/<child-id>` at `HEAD` with `git update-ref`, then return
      `{"success": False, "reset": False, "preserved_ref": "refs/wip/<child-id>",
      "preserved_commit": <tip>, "reason": …}` — no destructive command runs.
  - `phase_drive`: on a refused reset carrying `preserved_ref`, record
    `report["preserved_refs"]` (list of `{id, ref, commit}`), comment the ref +
    commit on the child, and stop the chain naming the real step/reason. No
    session is spawned for that child.
  - `_emit_phase_report` prints `preserved_refs` in the human summary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a worktree whose `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch,
   `_reset_child_worktree` returns `success: False`, `reset: False`,
   `preserved_ref == "refs/wip/<child-id>"` and `preserved_commit` equal to the
   worktree tip; neither `git reset --hard` nor `git clean -fd` ran.
2. `git rev-parse refs/wip/<child-id>` resolves to the tip after the refused
   reset, the original commit is still reachable from the worktree branch, and
   the ref does **not** appear in `git branch` output or `git worktree list`.
3. The preservation ref is created **before** any destructive command: a
   refused reset leaves the ref in place and the worktree byte-identical.
4. A worktree that is only uncommitted-dirty (no commits ahead) still takes the
   existing reset path and succeeds — behaviour unchanged, and the reset still
   uses `git clean -fd` **without** `-x` (ignored files such as the
   `node_modules` symlink survive; test asserts the flag).
5. `phase_drive` reports `preserved_refs` for the refused child, comments the
   `wip/<id>` ref and commit hash on the child, spawns no session for it, and
   the chain-stop message names the failing `finish` step and reason.
6. The existing isolation gates (main-checkout refusal, missing worktree,
   `--show-toplevel` mismatch) are unchanged and still covered by their current
   tests.
7. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
8. **Parent AC3 traceability.** **A worktree carrying commits is never reset.** `_reset_child_worktree` refuses when the child worktree's `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch; the tip is preserved on `refs/wip/<child-id>` **before** any destructive git command, and the ref + commit hash are reported in the drive report and commented on the child. Test: a real in-repo git worktree fixture proves (a) ahead-of-parent → no reset, `wip/<id>` resolves to the tip, original commit still reachable from the worktree branch; (b) only-uncommitted-dirty → existing reset still happens. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the ahead-of-parent refusal test and the uncommitted-only regression
   test first (they must fail), using the `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture.
2. Add the preservation gate between the isolation gates and the reset.
3. Thread `child_id` into `_reset_child_worktree` from `phase_drive`.
4. Record `preserved_refs`, comment on the child, extend `_emit_phase_report`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_reset_child_worktree` (~8148),
  `phase_drive` reset path (~9028–9095), `_emit_phase_report` (~8270).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestNonTerminalResetForRetry`
  (~646) extended with preservation cases.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — WIP-preservation ref (completed in
  the docs item).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Stale `wip/<id>` refs accumulate.** *Mitigation:* created only when a
  commit would otherwise be discarded; named in the report and the child
  comment; cleanup documented in the skill reference (docs item).
- **A ref name colliding with a real branch.** *Mitigation:* `refs/wip/<id>` is
  a fully qualified ref outside `refs/heads/`, so it never appears in `git
  branch` or worktree discovery.

## Dependencies

- `Test harness: refusal scripting and commit-carrying worktree` — supplies the
  ahead-of-parent fixture and the destructive-command recorder.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC3 (primary); establishes the no-commits-ahead invariant that
AC4's reset-for-retry slice documents.

data.description:
## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want `reset-for-retry` to apply only
to a worktree that holds **no** commits, and its audit comment to name exactly
what was discarded (a file list, never a commit hash), so a retained commit is
never implied to have been thrown away and an uncommitted discard is fully
documented (parent AC4).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: the `reset-for-retry` path is only reachable when
    `_reset_child_worktree` succeeded, which (after the preservation-gate item)
    implies the worktree carried no commits ahead of the parent branch. Pin that
    invariant in the code with an explicit guard/assert and in a test.
  - `_reset_for_retry_comment`: build the "discarded" section from the actual
    removed paths (`git clean -fd` output and/or `git status --porcelain=v1`
    captured before the reset), list them as a file list, and state explicitly
    that no commit was discarded. The comment must contain **no** commit hash
    token.
  - `_reset_child_worktree`: return the pre-reset `status --porcelain` paths in
    the result (`discarded_paths`) so the comment is evidence-based rather than
    inferred from `clean` stdout alone.
- Interpretation note to record on the parent: the parent item's "re-queue a
  finish-only retry rather than a session reset" is satisfied by the
  infrastructure-retry path (an infra refusal re-runs `parent` → `finish`
  against the preserved commit without spawning a session); a **gate** failure
  on a commit-carrying worktree stops the chain, because a finish-only retry
  would contradict parent AC6 (one attempt at the default bound).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A commit-carrying worktree whose `finish` exhausts the gate bound produces
   no `reset-for-retry` entry in `children_driven`, spawns no session, and
   reports `preserved_refs` for that child (test asserts all three).
2. `_reset_for_retry_comment` lists the discarded paths individually (one per
   line or a comma-separated list) derived from the pre-reset `git status
   --porcelain` / `git clean` output, and the comment body matches no 7–40
   character hex token that could be read as a commit hash (test asserts
   against a regex and against the preserved commit hash value).
3. When the worktree held no commits, the comment explicitly states that no
   commit was discarded, and its discarded-file list matches the files the
   reset actually removed (fixture comparison).
4. An infrastructure refusal on a commit-carrying worktree re-runs `parent`
   (finish-only, `sessions_spawned` unchanged) and never resets the worktree —
   pinned by a test.
5. Existing reset-for-retry behaviour for an uncommitted-dirty worktree is
   unchanged: reset succeeds, the child returns to `open`, and the loop
   continues with a fresh session.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC4 traceability.** **Reset-for-retry remains only for uncommitted WIP.** The retained reset path is unchanged when the worktree holds no commits, and its comment names exactly what was discarded (file list only — never a commit hash). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the comment-content tests first (no hex token, explicit
   no-commit-discarded statement, file list matches the fixture's discarded
   files).
2. Capture pre-reset `status --porcelain` in `_reset_child_worktree` and return
   `discarded_paths`.
3. Rebuild `_reset_for_retry_comment` around `discarded_paths`.
4. Add the explicit invariant guard on the reset-for-retry path.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_reset_for_retry_comment` (~8241),
  `_reset_child_worktree` (~8148), `phase_drive` reset path (~9028–9095).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestNonTerminalResetForRetry`
  (~646), comment-content assertions.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Comment regression (file list vs commit hash).** *Mitigation:* the test
  asserts the absence of any hash-shaped token, so a later edit that leaks a
  commit hash fails loudly.

## Dependencies

- `Commit-preservation gate before any reset` — establishes the
  no-commits-ahead invariant this item documents and pins.
- `Infra-retry budget for transient finish refusals` — supplies the
  finish-only retry path asserted in AC4.

## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want every drive verdict message and
child comment to name the failing `finish` step and reason — plus the
main-checkout lock holder and/or the offending paths and competing work item
when the report carries them — instead of the generic
`Failed to finish child <id>`, so I can tell an infrastructure refusal from a
genuine gate failure without excavating subprocess stdout (parent AC5).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - Add `_describe_finish_failure(finish_failure)` → `"<step>: <reason>"`
    plus optional `"; lock held by <holder>"` and
    `"; offending paths: <paths>; competing work item <id> (pid <n>)"`.
  - Use it in every drive verdict:
    - `infra-retry` (report message + `children_driven` entry + child comment),
    - `reset-for-retry` (report message + child comment),
    - `terminal-reconciled` (report message + child comment),
    - chain-stop / `failed_child` messages (bound exhausted, reset refused,
      reset-then-fail-again, status-reset failure).
  - Read the evidence from the threaded `finish_failure` payload:
    `steps.main_checkout_lock.holder`, `steps.main_checkout_guard.offending`,
    and `_main_checkout_actor_evidence` (competing work item + pid).
  - `_emit_phase_report` human summary prints the same evidence.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the message-shape sentence in the drive recovery
  section (full rewrite in the docs item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the four drive verdicts (`infra-retry`, `reset-for-retry`,
   `terminal-reconciled`, chain-stop) produces a message containing
   `"<step>: <reason>"` (e.g. `local_dev_fast_forward: local_dev_diverged`);
   a test asserts the substring for each verdict.
2. When the finish report carries `steps.main_checkout_lock.holder`, the
   message names the holder; when `steps.main_checkout_guard` carries offending
   paths and actor evidence, the message names the offending paths and the
   competing work item/pid (tests assert each).
3. The generic `Failed to finish child <id>` never appears alone in a drive
   message when a classified `finish_failure` is available (test asserts the
   generic text is absent or suffixed with the evidence).
4. The child comments for `reset-for-retry`, `terminal-reconciled`,
   `infra-retry` and chain-stop carry the same step/reason evidence (tests
   assert the comment bodies).
5. `_emit_phase_report`'s human output prints the evidence for the failing
   child (test asserts the rendered text).
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC5 traceability.** **The real step and reason are surfaced.** Drive's `reset-for-retry`, `terminal-reconciled`, `infra-retry` and chain-stop messages name the failing `finish` step and reason (plus the main-checkout lock holder and/or offending paths and competing work item when the report carries them), instead of the generic `Failed to finish child <id>`. Test: report/comment assertions for each verdict. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write one assertion per verdict first (they must fail on the generic text).
2. Add `_describe_finish_failure` and thread it through the four verdicts.
3. Extend `_emit_phase_report`.

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — drive recovery message shape.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Message bloat / noisy reports.** *Mitigation:* one shared formatter, one

- **Prose parsing re-enters through the back door.** *Mitigation:* every field

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the no-regression and termination properties of the
refusal-aware drive pinned by tests, so a genuine gate failure still stops the
chain at `--finish-attempt-limit` with no infrastructure retry, a
commit-carrying worktree is never reset, and drive always terminates (parent
AC6).

## Scope

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new `TestGateFailureRegression`
  and `TestDriveTermination`.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — CLI-flag default and loop-bound assertions
  for `--infra-retry-limit`.
- No production changes expected; if a test exposes a real defect, fix it in
  the owning slice rather than here (and record that on this item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `tests: tests_failed` finish failure (classified `gate`) at the default
   `--finish-attempt-limit` yields exactly one `finish` attempt, an empty
   `infra_retries`, no reset of a commit-carrying worktree, and a stop message
   naming `tests: tests_failed`.
2. A worktree-placement-violation finish failure likewise stops with no
   infrastructure retry and a stop message naming the failing step.
3. An unlisted `(step, reason)` pair (`unknown`) counts against the gate bound
   (`finish_attempts` increments, `infra_retries` stays empty).
4. Termination: with `--infra-retry-limit 5` and `--finish-attempt-limit 1`, an
   always-infrastructure-refusing harness terminates — the recorded `parent`
   invocation count equals `infra_retry_limit + finish_attempt_limit`
   (+ the terminal classification pass), `success` is `false`,
   `failed_child` is set, and no session was spawned.
5. Termination under mixed failure kinds: alternating gate and infrastructure
   failures also terminate within the combined bound.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC6 traceability.** **No regression for genuine gate failures.** A tests-failed (or worktree-placement) `finish` still stops the chain at `--finish-attempt-limit` with **no** infrastructure retry, and drive always terminates (the loop bound accounts for the infrastructure retry budget). Test: scripted gate-failure harness asserts one attempt at the default bound, no reset of a commit-carrying worktree, and a stop message naming the failing step. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

   infra-retry slice; if it fails, the classification branch is wrong).
2. Add the termination test counting `parent` invocations via
   `RecordingParent.returned`.
3. Add the mixed-kind termination test.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator or maintainer, I want the drive recovery contract documented —
the classification vocabulary, the `--infra-retry-limit` flag and backoff, the
`refs/wip/<id>` preservation ref and its cleanup, and the new report fields —
including the `scripts/install_pi.sh` reinstall step, so the shipped behaviour
and its docs cannot drift (parent AC7, AC8).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — rewrite §"A failing `finish` is bounded,
  reconciled, then reset (SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY)" to cover: the classifier and
  its `infrastructure`/`gate`/`unknown` kinds; `--infra-retry-limit` (default
  `5`, backoff 2 s doubling to a 30 s cap); the commit-preservation gate and
  `refs/wip/<id>`; the new report fields; and that `unknown` fails safe.
  Keep the existing anchor target for
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md#drive-failure-recovery-…` valid.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — extend §"Drive failure recovery":
  - the full `(step, reason) → kind` vocabulary table mirroring the code
    constant;
  - retry semantics (`finish_attempts` vs `infra_retries`, both bounds, the
    backoff schedule, no session spawn);
  - WIP preservation: ref naming, when it is created, how to inspect
    (`git rev-parse`, `git log --oneline -1 refs/wip/<id>`), and cleanup
    (`git update-ref -d refs/wip/<id>`) — explicitly **not** automatic;
  - the report surface additions (`finish_failure`, `infra_retries`,
    `infra_retry_limit`, `preserved_refs`, `result: "infra-retry"`,
    `result: "finish-only-retry"` if shipped) and the guarantee that existing
    keys keep their meaning/types;
  - the reinstall step: canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/`;
    `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` is the installed runtime copy and must
    never be edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` (new) — doc/code consistency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md`'s drive-recovery section documents the
   classifier kinds, the `--infra-retry-limit` flag with its default and
   backoff, the commit-preservation gate / `refs/wip/<id>`, and the new report
   fields; the existing cross-reference anchor still resolves.
2. `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` §"Drive failure recovery" carries a
   `(step, reason) → kind` table whose rows match the code's
   `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` constants exactly.
3. A doc/code consistency test fails if the code constant and the reference
   table diverge in either direction (a new emitted reason or a stale doc row).
4. The reference documents `refs/wip/<id>` creation, inspection and cleanup,
   stating that cleanup is manual, and documents the reinstall step plus the
   "never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`" rule.
5. The documented report fields match the keys the drive report actually emits
   (test asserts each documented new key is present in a produced report, and
   each pre-existing key still has its original type); no documented field is
   unshipped (no forward-looking keys).
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC7 traceability.** **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (drive recovery section, the `--infra-retry-limit` flag, the new report fields) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ("Drive failure recovery" section: classification vocabulary, WIP-preservation ref, retry semantics). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.
8. **Parent AC8 traceability.** **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (dev-push gate), and the reinstall step is documented: the canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/`; `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` is the installed runtime copy and must **not** be edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the doc/code consistency test first (it must fail before the doc
   table exists).
2. Extend the reference doc section.
3. Rewrite the `SKILL.md` drive-recovery section, preserving the anchor.
4. Add the report-surface assertions.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — drive recovery section (~648).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Drive failure recovery" (~263).
- `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` (new).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Vocabulary drift between code and docs.** *Mitigation:* the consistency
  test fails on any divergence in either direction (parent risk register).
- **Documenting `~/.pi/agent/skills` as editable.** *Mitigation:* AC4 asserts
  the "never edit the runtime copy" statement is present.

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading`
- `Infra-retry budget for transient finish refusals`
- `Commit-preservation gate before any reset`
- `Surface the real step, reason and evidence in drive verdicts`

Parent AC7 (primary) and AC8's reinstall/never-edit-the-runtime-copy
documentation; the full-suite part of AC8 is enforced by the dev-push gate.
